title: Compact Audit Agent and Exporter Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines the lightweight evidence collection agent ("compact agent"), the compact SIEM exporter protocol, and the operational workflows for control-evidence capture under RBAC v2. It is intended for engineering teams shipping agents to Dedicated and Private deployments, security engineers who onboard new controls, and SREs who run the exporter fleet.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: local collectors (agent process/container), short-term buffer/cache, integrity stamping, compact audit record schema, batching + transport to SIEM (HTTPS/syslog), RBAC v2 lookup behavior, minimal local policy for PII redaction, health telemetry, and runbook playflows for common failures.
- Non-goals: full forensic chain-of-custody tooling (separate repo), long-term cold storage design, or deep SIEM-specific normalization (we export compact canonical records; SIEM teams map on ingest).

High-level architecture (informal):
- Agent runs as a privileged minimal process on host/container.
- Local input adapters: application audit socket, nginx audit hook, orchestration webhooks, k8s audit proxy. Each adapter normalizes into the Compact Audit Record (CAR) struct.
- Agent pipeline: normalize -> enrich (env, cluster, agent_id) -> RBAC v2 resolution (actor -> roles -> allowed evidence labels) -> redact (policy) -> sign (HMAC with local key) -> buffer -> export.
- Exporters: HTTPS JSON endpoint (preferred), Syslog/TLS fallback. Export batches respecting size/time thresholds.

Compact Audit Record (CAR) - canonical fields (required minimal set):
- car_id: string (uuid4)
- ts: string (ISO8601 UTC)
- src: string (adapter id, e.g., k8s-audit, app-socket)
- actor_id: string (user/service principal id)
- actor_type: string (user | service | system)
- action: string (create|read|update|delete|auth|config_change|exec|other)
- target: string (resource identifier, e.g., model:1234, keyring:prod)
- outcome: string (success|failure|unknown)
- request_id: string (trace/request id if available)
- labels: list of strings (e.g., control:s3-read, pii:maybe)
- evidence_flags: list of strings (e.g., evidence_required, transient, high_entropy)
- payload_digest: string (sha256 of relevant payload after redact)
- redaction_applied: list of strings (fields redacted) or empty list
- agent_id: string (id of collector binary instance)
- signature: string (HMAC-SHA256 over canonicalized CAR)
- raw_excerpt: string (optional short context snippet, max 4k chars)

Notes: CAR is intentionally compact. SIEM teams should enrich on ingest with IP/geo, org metadata, and mapping to their canonical field names. The payload_digest enables dedupe across buffering/replay.

RBAC v2 resolution behavior (integration guidance):
- Lookup is eventually-consistent and cached locally for 2 minutes by default. Agents query the control-plane RBAC endpoint or a local signed snapshot file (recommended for air-gapped).
- Resolution result typed as allow/deny/conditional. Conditional results carry conditions that become enforcement-time labels on the CAR (e.g., conditional:requires-mfa -> labels: [conditional:mfa]).
- If RBAC cannot be queried (timeout or unreachable), agent uses 'fail-open-to-log' policy by default but marks the CAR with labels: [rbac:unknown, exported_under_fallback]. Site SAs may opt-in to fail-closed via agent config.

PII and redaction policies (minimal local rules):
- Agents apply conservative redaction for fields matching regexes for emails, long hex keys, full credit-card patterns, and OAuth tokens.
- Operators can provide per-adapter redaction allowlists (fields permitted through).
- Redaction should replace values with tokens like <<REDACTED:EMAIL>> and add the field name to redaction_applied.

Signing and proof-of-origin:
- Agents sign CARs with an HMAC key derived from an agent private key stored in the host KMS or a file protected by node-level permissions.
- Signature covers the canonicalized CAR fields (sorted keys, predictable ordering).
- Exporter verifies signature optional on ingest. When using private deployments, SIEM teams should enable signature verification.

Transport and batching rules:
- Default batch size: 250 CARs or 512KB, whichever is first.
- Max batch latency: 3s in low-latency mode, 30s in cost-saving mode.
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, retry up to 5 times. Persistent failures move batch to disk-backed queue and emit alert if queue > 50MB.
- Backpressure: if exporter endpoint returns 429 or 5xx repeatedly, agent enters jittered backoff and switches to local disk queue.

Compact SIEM Export protocol (HTTPS JSON):
- POST /v1/compact-audit/batch
- Headers: X-Agent-Id, X-Agent-Version, X-Cluster-Id, Authorization: Bearer <mTLS or API token> (deployments should prefer mTLS).
- Body: JSON array of CAR objects.
- Response: 200 OK {"ingested": n, "skipped": m} or 207 Partial with per-index errors.
- Recommended TLS: TLS1.3 and mutual TLS for private deployments.

Syslog/TLS fallback:
- RFC5424 framing, with message body a compressed (gzip) JSON array of CARs. Use TLS and server cert pinning where possible. Syslog receivers will decompress and pass to normalization pipeline.

Deduplication and idempotency:
- Use car_id and payload_digest to dedupe. SIEM ingest should maintain short-lived index of recent car_id or digest (48–72 hours) to catch replays from restarts/backfills.

Backfill and replay:
- Agents support a replay mode that replays archived CAR batches from local disk or object storage. Batches replayed must set header X-Replay: true and include original_ts for the batch; signer must be present. SIEM ingestion should treat replayed data as higher-weight evidence but not duplicate counts.

Operational telemetry and SLOs (agent-level):
- Metrics exposed: queued_batches, exported_batches, export_failures, last_success_ts, rbactime_ms, redactions_count, disk_queue_bytes.
- Health probe: /health returns 200 with JSON including last_export_status and disk_queue_bytes.
- SLOs: 99.9% of CARs exported within 30s under normal network conditions; 99% of agent heartbeats within 15s.

Runbook: common incident flows (short):
- Exporter HTTP 401/403:
  - Check agent credentials (mTLS certs expired, token rotated).
  - Verify clock skew (>5s leads to signature failures).
  - Remedy: rotate token, rotate cert, restart agent.
- Persistent 5xx / 429:
  - Agent should buffer to disk. Alert on queue size; identify upstream SIEM issues. Temporary mitigation: switch to secondary exporter endpoint (configurable).
- RBAC lookup failures causing excessive 'rbac:unknown' labels:
  - Investigate control-plane RBAC endpoint; consider increasing local cache TTL for stability; mark as degraded.
- Disk queue growth > 200MB:
  - Eviction policy: oldest non-critical records are expired first (policy controlled). Consider increasing retention or provisioning more exporter capacity.

Deployment checklist (for Dedicated/Private):
- Confirm KMS or keystore for agent signing keys is accessible.
- Configure RBAC snapshot or control-plane access for the cluster.
- Register agent_id with inventory service and set expected version.
- Provide SIEM teams with exporter endpoint, mTLS cert, and ingestion key.
- Run smoke tests that assert: CARs arrive, signatures validate, dedupe works, replay header honored.

Testing and QA guidance:
- Unit tests for adapter normalizers, redaction regexes, and signing routine.
- Integration tests with a local SIEM stub that validates batched ingest, partial failures, and 207 handling.
- Fuzz tests for oversized fields and malformed adapter inputs.

Privacy and compliance considerations:
- Default conservative redaction minimizes PII in transit.
- For regulated customers, provide config knob to never export raw_excerpt.
- Retention: agents only cache transient data; long-term retention policies are managed on the SIEM/archive side.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Standardizing a minimal set of control labels for mapping to compliance controls (ISO/PCI/SOC) — propose an RFC with compliance team.
- Should we include an optional small public-key signature bundle for cross-org verification?
- Investigate embedding a lightweight proofchain anchor to a central ledger for high-value evidence.

Appendix: short example CAR (pretty-printed):
{
  "car_id": "7f9c2e8a-4e1b-4c6f-a123-9f0b1c4d5e6f",
  "ts": "2025-09-18T15:32:02Z",
  "src": "k8s-audit",
  "actor_id": "svc:deploy-agent@redwood",
  "actor_type": "service",
  "action": "update",
  "target": "deployment:inference-api-prod",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_id": "trace-9933a7",
  "labels": ["control:deployment-change", "env:prod"],
  "evidence_flags": ["evidence_required"],
  "payload_digest": "sha256:abcd1234...",
  "redaction_applied": [],
  "agent_id": "agent-nyc-01",
  "signature": "hmac:...",
  "raw_excerpt": "patch: image updated from x to y"
}

Notes about uniqueness: this playbook emphasizes a deliberately compact canonical record (CAR) and a pragmatic exporter protocol sized for high-throughput Dedicated fleets and constrained Private deployments. It blends runbook steps and engineering spec fragments to match Drive style (working doc).
